title: Alibi and Parish
premise: When the coffin of Aldous Parish, founder of the fog-bound town of Dravenmoor Hollow, is exhumed for a heritage ceremony and found empty, true-crime podcaster Jude Dravenmoor is pulled into a case that predates his own family's arrival. The empty grave unravels a 60-year-old disappearance, an inheritance scheme built on a fabricated death, and a killer who has been curating the town's memory for decades. As Jude investigates, he realizes the killer knows every detail of the case file because they wrote it—someone inside the parish records office who has been erasing and rewriting history to protect the inheritance of Parish's fortune. The climax comes when Jude stages a fake exhumation of a second grave, forcing the killer to destroy evidence in real time; the resolution reveals the killer is the town historian, Parish's secret daughter, who never belonged anywhere until she decided belonging meant owning the story itself.
about_author: Wendell Nakamura is a former small-town archivist who spent a decade cataloguing municipal records before turning to fiction, giving his mysteries an unnerving authenticity about paper trails and buried secrets. He lives on the Pacific coast, where he records ambient soundscapes of coastal towns that often find their way into his atmospheric prose.

chapters.title: The Weight of Empty Earth
chapters.summary: Jude Dravenmoor, POV. On the morning of the heritage exhumation, Jude watches from the crowd as workers lift Aldous Parish's coffin—and find it filled with river stones. His recorder captures the gasp of three hundred townspeople. Emotional beat: the thrill of a live mystery colliding with dread, because Jude came here seeking anonymity after solving three 'accidents' that made him a target.

chapters.title: A Town That Remembers Wrong
chapters.summary: Jude, POV. He interviews townsfolk at the wake and notices everyone tells the same story about Parish with identical phrasing—as if rehearsed. The parish records office refuses him access. Emotional beat: unease deepening into fascination as Jude realizes the town's collective memory has been curated, not preserved.

chapters.title: Three Accidents and a Podcast
chapters.summary: Jude, POV, with flashback structure. He reviews his own back catalog: the three deaths he solved, the threats that followed, why he fled to Dravenmoor Hollow. Emotional beat: guilt and self-protection—he swore off cases, yet the empty coffin hooks something he can't switch off.

chapters.title: The Historian's Ledger
chapters.summary: Introduce Maren Voss, the town historian, POV. She catalogs the exhumation fallout with unsettling calm, noting discrepancies in her ledger. A visitor asks questions she answers too smoothly. Emotional beat: controlled menace—the reader senses Maren is managing information without knowing exactly what she's hiding.

chapters.title: Grave Registration 1958
chapters.summary: Jude, POV. Using a retired gravedigger's memory and a forged research permit, Jude learns the burial record was amended twice: once in 1964, once last year. Emotional beat: triumph curdling into fear—someone altered official records recently, meaning the killer is active, not historical.

chapters.title: What the Stones Were For
chapters.summary: Maren, POV. She traces where the river stones came from—a quarry closed in 1959, the same year Parish vanished from public life. She burns a page of her ledger. Emotional beat: complicity tightening; Maren's loyalty to someone unnamed costs her sleep.

chapters.title: The Inheritance Nobody Claimed
chapters.summary: Jude, POV. Court archives reveal Parish's estate passed to a trust administered by the parish council, paying annual stipends to founding families—including Jude's own ancestors. Emotional beat: vertigo; Jude realizes he isn't an outsider investigating but a beneficiary whose family was bought into silence.

chapters.title: Fog on the Causeway
chapters.summary: Jude, POV. Someone runs him off the causeway road at night; his car ends up in the shallows. He survives, saves the dashcam audio—a second engine, then nothing. Emotional beat: terror converting curiosity into commitment; staying invisible is no longer possible or safe.

chapters.title: Letters to a Dead Man
chapters.summary: Maren, POV. We learn she has written letters to her father for forty years, unsent, stored in the archive basement. Her father is Aldous Parish. Emotional beat: grief exposed—the antagonist's humanity surfaces, complicating the reader's allegiance.

chapters.title: The Case File That Reads Itself
chapters.summary: Jude, POV. He obtains a leaked copy of the original 1958 investigation file and finds annotations in a hand he recognizes from the amended burial record. Whoever annotated it predicted every investigative dead end. Emotional beat: cold clarity—Jude isn't ahead of the killer; he's walking a path already mapped.

chapters.title: Founding Families, Founding Lies
chapters.summary: Jude, POV. Cross-referencing stipend ledgers with census data, he finds four founding families received payments conditioned on never discussing 1958. Two are now dead—the same two from his old podcast cases? No: coincidences unravel differently. Emotional beat: paranoia and pattern-hunger, Jude's gift becoming his liability.

chapters.title: The Second Grave
chapters.summary: Maren, POV. She visits a second, unmarked grave on Parish land and speaks to it like a confession booth. Flashback: 1958, a night at the quarry, a body that wasn't her father's. Emotional beat: dread and tenderness entangled—the reader learns Parish may have killed someone, and Maren covered for a ghost.

chapters.title: An Alibi Made of Paper
chapters.summary: Jude, POV. He reconstructs how the killer built a perfect alibi: documents proving Parish died abroad in 1959 while the body in the coffin (now missing) was someone else entirely. Emotional beat: reluctant admiration for the killer's craft, sharpening Jude's resolve to beat them at archival warfare.

chapters.title: Trial Date Set
chapters.summary: Jude, POV. The DA, pressured by public outrage over the empty coffin, announces an inquest with trial to follow in six weeks. Jude realizes the killer must permanently bury the truth before sworn testimony begins. Emotional beat: ticking clock installed; every chapter now races toward the deadline.

chapters.title: The Archivist Confesses, Sort Of
chapters.summary: Maren, POV. Under gentle pressure from Jude, Maren gives a half-confession about falsifying records—but frames herself as protecting the town from a worse truth. Emotional beat: tragic self-justification; she believes she is the town's immune system.

chapters.title: Who Belongs Here
chapters.summary: Jude, POV. Digging into adoption and baptismal registers, Jude confirms Maren Voss was born Maren Parish, hidden away, disinherited by a father who chose reputation over her. Emotional beat: heartbreak reframing the hunt—Jude understands the motive now, and understanding makes stopping her harder.

chapters.title: Night in the Records Basement
chapters.summary: Jude, POV. Breaking into the archive basement, Jude finds Maren's letters and the original coffin's contents hidden behind shelving: Parish's actual remains, plus a second skeleton's personal effects. Maren catches him there. Emotional beat: confrontation suspended between violence and recognition—two people who both need the truth told differently.

chapters.title: The Story She Owed Him
chapters.summary: Maren, POV. She holds Jude at knifepoint and instead talks: her father faked his death to escape a murder he committed at the quarry, letting an innocent man fill his coffin. Maren spent her life guarding the lie that let her exist. Emotional beat: full tragic reveal; the killer's logic becomes almost persuasive.

chapters.title: Trap of Ash and Paper
chapters.summary: Jude, POV. Jude leaks word of a second exhumation at the unmarked grave. Maren must go destroy the evidence herself; Jude records her tampering live, streaming to the town square screens. Emotional beat: cathartic reversal—the invisible man makes the killer visible to everyone at once.

chapters.title: Inquest
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs, courtroom structure. Maren, arrested, chooses to testify fully, narrating 1958 in open court while the town hears its founding myth dismantled. Jude testifies to the paper trail. Emotional beat: grim vindication shadowed by sorrow—justice arrives, but it indicts the whole town's willing amnesia.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Jude, POV. Aftermath: the trust dissolved, stipends ended, founding families furious at losing comfort. Jude visits Maren in custody; she asks if the podcast will tell her side. He promises the whole story, not a flattering one. Emotional beat: quiet mercy within accountability.

chapters.title: Alibi and Parish
chapters.summary: Jude, POV. Months later, Jude releases the final episode—not exposing the town but returning its true history to it. He decides to stay in Dravenmoor Hollow, no longer hiding. Final image: he places flowers on the unmarked grave of the man who died in Parish's place, finally named. Emotional beat: belonging earned through truth rather than inherited through silence.
